summary.title: Linux Performance
summary.one_liner: A curated index of Brendan Gregg's Linux performance tools, posts, talks and recommended resources, covering observability, tracing (ftrace, perf, eBPF/bcc/bpftrace), flame graphs and tuning.
keywords: how do i analyze linux performance
takeaways: Start with the first ten commands in 'Linux Performance Analysis in 60,000 Milliseconds' for a quick investigation workflow.
Learn the main Linux performance tool families: perf, ftrace (perf-tools), and eBPF (bcc, bpftrace).
Use the recommended talks, in order, as a tour from fundamentals (LISA 2019) to advanced tracing and profiling.
Read the posts on load averages, frame pointers and off-CPU analysis to understand specific metrics and methods.
summary.summary: This page is a link collection by Brendan Gregg covering Linux performance material he created, plus some third-party resources. It groups content into tools (perf, eBPF tools, perf-tools, bcc, bpftrace, Flame Graphs), documentation (articles on the 60-second analysis checklist, load averages, frame pointers, EC2 tuning and many eBPF/ftrace posts), talks ranked from introductory to advanced, and external resources such as the RHEL performance guide. It also links printable tool maps for observability, static analysis, benchmarking, tuning and sar. The page itself contains no tutorial steps; it works as an index to the linked material.
